_transcription: PAGE MAP - 11 rendered pages (idx 0..10 = printed folios 1..11), every index accounted for. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series A1BAB/2, SET-2, Q.P. Code 55/2/2, 'PHYSICS (Theory)', Time 2 hours, Maximum Marks 35, '11 printed pages', '12 questions'). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (folios 3, 5, 7, 9, 11). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. As on the 55/2/1 opener, the HINDI page PRECEDES its English twin. NO overflow of one language onto the other's page, no parity inversion, and idx 10 (the last page) is English. That was MEASURED, not read off the contact sheet: a first probe counting Devanagari codepoints was WRONG and reported all 11 pages as English, because this booklet sets Hindi in a LEGACY NON-UNICODE font whose glyphs map onto ASCII (idx 5 extracts as 'AZw MaU aVr BgHo'). Re-run as a real-English-word ratio with a self-test on strings from these very pages, the split is total: English pages score 0.57-0.94 and all five Hindi pages score EXACTLY 0.00 - not one real English word, so no English block spills onto any of them. STRUCTURE agrees exactly with the printed General Instructions on idx 2: 12 questions / three sections / A = Q1-3 @2, B = Q4-11 @3, C = Q12 case study @5, total 35. ** THE PAPER IS NOT MCQ-FREE. ** Q12's five case-study sub-parts (a)-(e) are four-option MCQs printed '5x1=5', and the marking scheme keys them in its own Section-C table as a)(iii) b)(iv) c)(ii) d)(iii) e)(iv), read by vision off ms/p09 and mapped positionally (i)-(iv) -> A-D. Sections A and B are entirely subjective and there is no Section-A key to read. INTERNAL CHOICE: exactly THREE (Q1, Q7, Q8), established THREE independent ways - a printed 'OR' on the English page (idx 4 for Q1; idx 6 for Q7 and Q8), a printed 'अथवा' on its Hindi twin (idx 3 for Q1; idx 5 for Q7 and Q8, both confirmed at magnification), and exactly three bare 'OR' lines on their own in the marking scheme (ms p02, p06, p07). The scheme's 'Alternatively:-' (Q1a), '(Any two of the above or any two other uses)' (Q2), '(Or Any other)' (Q7a) and 'Ultraviolet/Visible/Infrared (either)' (Q7b) are answer-equivalences, not choices, and are correctly excluded. Q6, Q9, Q10 and Q11 print (a)/(b) sub-parts with NO 'OR' and are one row each. Primary branches sum to 6+24+5 = 35. DECIMAL POINTS: this paper prints RAISED dots - confirmed two ways, visually at 3.5x on '55·93494' / '27·98191' and, independently, by the text layer of the English page idx 4, where U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT is the ONLY non-ASCII codepoint that survives at all - so stems use {\cdot}. Note the MARKING SCHEME prints ordinary baseline dots for the same numbers ('55.93494 - 2 x 27.98191'); the paper is followed, per the addendum. FIGURES: this paper prints ONE, the energy-level diagram in Q9 (idx 6), and it is REQUIRED. That is a difference from the 55/2/1 opener, which prints none - the figure was read on THIS page rather than inherited. Every 'Depict / Draw a labelled ray diagram / with the help of a circuit diagram / Depict the intensity distribution' instruction elsewhere is the STUDENT drawing, and the figures in the marking scheme are ANSWER figures. VOIDS: the whole ten-page marking scheme was scanned end to end and there is NO award-regardless note anywhere, no keyless void, no dual key, and no clause scoped to one language medium. The five notes it does print are all ordinary marking latitude, conditional on the student's work: 'Allot 1/2 Mark for only formula' (Q1a), 'Award 1 mark, if a student draws a diagram showing depletion region' (Q3), 'If the student takes inverted input waveform full credit to be given' (Q4), 'Give full credit to any other use written' (Q7b) and a DEDUCTION note on Q8a. MERGED MARKING SCHEME: the source file is 'XII_042_MS__55_2-(1 & 2 & 3).pdf', covering 55/2/1, 55/2/2 and 55/2/3. The rendered range was confirmed to be exactly 55/2/2's ten pages by their own printed footers - every page reads '042_55/2/2_Physics # Page-N' for N = 1..10 - so no key or void can have been read off a sibling paper.

questions.stem: Photoelectric emission occurs when a surface is irradiated with the radiation of frequency (i) \(v_1\), and (ii) \(v_2\). The maximum kinetic energy of the electrons emitted in the two cases are K and 2K respectively. Obtain the expression for the threshold frequency for the surface.
questions._flag: The two frequencies are printed as an italic LATIN 'v' with a subscript, not the Greek nu that the quantity normally carries. Transcribed AS PRINTED. Measured on THIS paper's own text layer rather than inherited from the sibling set: on English page idx 4 every Greek glyph and the degree sign that are visibly printed DROP from the text layer (alpha, both thetas and both degree signs of Q1(a) all extract as nothing), while these two characters survive extraction as ASCII 'v' (U+0076) - so they are set in the body font, not the Symbol font. The marking scheme, by contrast, sets the same quantity as a proper Greek nu throughout its worked answer. No effect on answerability; the quantity is unambiguously frequency.

Find the ratio of the de Broglie wavelengths associated with an alpha particle and a proton, if both
(a) have the same speeds,
(b) have the same kinetic energy,
(c) are accelerated through the same potential difference.

(a) Depict the variation of the potential energy of a pair of nucleons with the separation between them.
(b) Imagine the fission of a \({}^{56}_{26}\mathrm{Fe}\) into two equal fragments of \({}^{28}_{13}\mathrm{Al}\) nucleus. Is the fission energetically possible ? Justify your answer by working out Q value of the process.
Given : \(m\left({}^{56}_{26}\mathrm{Fe}\right) = 55{\cdot}93494\) u, \(m\left({}^{28}_{13}\mathrm{Al}\right) = 27{\cdot}98191\) u.

questions.stem:
(a) State Bohr's quantization condition for defining stationary orbits.
(b) Use the energy level diagram shown below to obtain the relation between three wavelengths \(\lambda_1\), \(\lambda_2\) and \(\lambda_3\) emitted due to the transition of electron from the energy states C and B.
questions._figure: REQUIRED - the relation the question asks for follows entirely from which pair of levels each wavelength labels, and the stem names none of them, so part (b) is unanswerable from the text alone. LAYOUT, described: three horizontal energy levels drawn one above another and labelled, at their right-hand ends, C at the top, B in the middle and A at the bottom; three vertical downward arrows run between levels, each tagged with one of \(\lambda_1\), \(\lambda_2\), \(\lambda_3\). WITHHELD deliberately: which pair of levels each arrow joins, because that assignment IS the answer. Page idx 6.

(b) the critical angle for the prism.

questions.context: The British physicist Thomas Young explained the interference of light using the principle of superposition of waves. He observed the interference pattern on the screen, in his experimental set-up, known now as Young's double slit experiment. The two slits \(\mathrm{S_1}\) and \(\mathrm{S_2}\) were illuminated by light from a slit S. The interference pattern consists of dark and bright bands of light. Such bands are called fringes. The distance between two consecutive bright and dark fringes is called fringe width.
questions.stem: If the screen is moved closer to the plane of slits \(\mathrm{S_1}\) and \(\mathrm{S_2}\), then the fringe width :

options.label: A
options.text: will decrease, but the intensity of bright fringe remains the same.

options.label: B
options.text: will increase, but the intensity of bright fringe decreases.

options.label: C
options.text: will decrease, but the intensity of bright fringe increases.

options.label: D
options.text: and the intensity both remain the same.
